cells.tense: Right now you are at the door of the new thing, and the read arrives without asking anything of you.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Once it's clear what to do about what's arrived, take the first step the same day. No writing the reasoning out to anyone first.
cells.core:
Whatever is entering your life right now — a job, a person, a decision — you get your read on it clean. It turns up already settled, and nothing in you is scrambling to make it so. You sit quiet long enough that it can surface, and that quiet is not the same as doubt. This is the part of you that holds a thing whole a moment before you say it.

The closing is already paid for: the hours of sitting through it by hand. So keep it. Once it's clear what to do about what's arrived, take the first step the same day. Next morning the thing will be in motion.
cells.sheetLine: The read arrives settled. It doesn't need defending.
cells.verb: weighing what you know before you speak it
cells.place: where what's entering is first met

cells.tense: Before the thing has finished arriving, you are already checking what it will do to you.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: Take one step on something arriving now and don't wait for a sign it will last — no asking anyone, no hunting for proof. Just the step.
cells.core:
Something is on its way in, and you're living at the far end of it first — rehearsing which way it goes, what it means, whether it holds. The read you'd get by just standing there is skipped for one you can't get yet. When you land, the timing comes free; from here, it can't.

Take one step on what's arriving and don't wait for a sign that it will last. No asking anyone, no hunting for more proof — just the step today. A thing that hasn't arrived yet can't tell you anything, and every projection costs you the version of it that's actually here.
cells.sheetLine: You're reading a thing that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.verb: weighing what you know before you speak it
cells.place: where what's entering is first met

cells.tense: The read came, and you waited at the door long after it had already opened.
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Take what you've already finished — the job done, the plan complete — and use it exactly as it is. Add nothing.
cells.core:
You stood in back of the moment — you knew, and you didn't say it. The new thing arrived and you met it a step behind your own feet. It's not that the read failed. It's that when the read came, you sat down with it and waited for something else to arrive first.

Take what you've already finished — the job done, the plan complete — and use it exactly as it is. Add nothing. The arrival was real. Touching a finished thing is how the next one gets a place to land, and it's cheaper than waiting for permission you don't owe anyone.
cells.sheetLine: The read came. You stayed at the door.

cells.tense: You are reading what's arriving correctly and calling the read the situation, not yours.
cells.act: accept what is offered for what you gave
cells.ask: When someone offers you something this week — help, their time, half of something — take it plainly, without working out what it costs you. Keep it.
cells.core:
There is a read arriving in you most days lately, and it's usually right. The person across the counter, the offer, the thing that isn't what it says — you catch it before you can name how. And when it's right, the credit goes to the facts, or the person, or the mood of the day. You don't see your hand. It's a sharp instrument, and you're carrying it without a sign.

When someone offers you something this week, take it plainly — their time, a hand, half of something — without working out what it costs you. Keep it once. This ability holds better when given back than when quietly explained away.
cells.sheetLine: The read is yours. The credit usually isn't.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that other people can see this knowing before it's said — the record gives decisive inner knowing, not a visible audience. The reader could reasonably say the knowing is slow, not early, or that nobody else notices. The ask survives — the act is the person's own, done alone — and it teaches whether or not the read is right. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is the Too Much line about being asked sooner than you can answer; it's sharper than the record supports.
